REQUEST
The applicant, Michael Zenon, has requested approval of final precise plans for a Planned
Assembly Development (PAD) for a 65-unit senior housing mixed-use development including
a day-care on a 26,250 square-foot C-2 (General Commercial)/Mixed-Use Overlay zoned
property at 3320 West 85th Street. The development would also include the replacement of
38 parking spaces on-site for the adjacent church and church administrative offices.

BACKGROUND
Chapter 12, Articles 4, 18, 22.1 and 25 of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC) require
approval of a Special Use Permit (SUP) for Planned Assembly Development (PAD) projects
with separate public hearings to consider approval of Preliminary and Final (precise)
development plans of a Planned Assembly Development.

The purpose of a PAD is to encourage more creative approaches to the development of land
than would be possible through the strict application of standard zoning regulations. It also
requires inter-departmental reviews and recommendations on all aspects of the proposal
prior to approval of final plans for the PAD. The PAD application is to include any requested
deviation from the regulations of the zone in which the site is located or from regulations that
would be applicable for the type of development being proposed. The proposed project is
discussed below with the areas of code compliance and deviations from the code.

On April 13, 2020 the Planning Commission adopted EA-MND-2019-120, Special Use Permit
No. 2019-013 (SP-2019-013) for a Preliminary Planned Assembly Development to allow a
five-story, 65-unit-senior mixed–use development (Resolution No. 1861) with 19 conditions
of approval and the following Code deviations:
A. Parking
    One (1) parking space per unit in-lieu of the Code-required 1.5 parking spaces per
  unit.
    Compact parking spaces in-lieu of the Code prohibition.
    Twelve (12) guest parking spaces in-lieu of the Code-required 22 parking spaces.
    Residential parking in tandem configuration in-lieu of the Code prohibition of
  tandem parking.
    Commercial parking spaces in tandem configuration in-lieu of the Code prohibition.
    Shared parking between of 18 parking spaces between the pre-school and church.
C. Open Space
    Provide a 53 square-foot balcony in-lieu of the Code-required minimum 80 square
  feet for 59 of the 65 proposed units.

To address the remaining conditions of approval and prior to being scheduled for a Final PAD
hearing, the applicant was required to receive preliminary approval for Site Plan Review
(SPR). On May 11, 2020 the applicant submitted the Site Plan Review application. During
the Site Plan Review, Staff determined that because the existing church and administrative
offices will remain on a separate lot from the proposed mixed-use development, a reduction
of building separation requirements is no longer needed as a code deviation. On September
25, 2020, Planning Staff found that the submitted plans with all required agency approvals

DISCUSSION
The 26,250 square-foot proposed mixed-use site is located midblock between 11th Avenue
and Crenshaw Drive. Currently, the existing site contains an approximately 2,300 square-
foot Chapel and an approximately 5,052 square-foot pre-school with an existing 11,214
square-foot play area. The chapel will be demolished along with the existing pre-school to
make way for the new development. Adjacent to these structures and proposed to remain
on a separate site are the church and church administrative offices.

Project Description
The five-story, 65-unit senior housing mixed use development will consist of 59 one-bedroom
units and six (6) two-bedroom units. Four (4) of the one-bedroom units which will be made
affordable at a low income affordability level. In addition to the units the development will
also include a 4,313 square-foot pre-school. The total number of units includes a PAD
density bonus, senior housing bonus and low-income affordable housing bonus. Table 1
below details the allowable unit calculation.

The basement level will provide residential parking. The first floor of the development will
consist of two units, the pre-school, residential lobby, residential amenity space that includes
a multipurpose room, a gym and a commercial kitchen as well as approximately 3,650 square
feet of common open space along 85th Street. The first floor will also provide residential and
visitor parking. The second floor will consist of all non-residential parking spaces. Floors
three (3) to five (5) will include two (2) residential unit types: Unit A (one-bedroom) and Unit
B (two bedroom). Each unit will include a living room, kitchen, bathroom and balcony. Unit A
floorplans will provide an approximately 53 square-foot balcony and Unit B floorplans will
provide an approximately 82 square-foot balcony. The third floor will also include a 2,234
square-foot landscaped deck that will also serve as common area for the residents. The
applicant will provide a 100 square-foot children’s play area on the main level adjacent to the
preschool playground.

The new 4,313 square-foot pre-school will have a 3,154 playground. Based on the size of
the playground, the pre-school will have a maximum enrollment of 42 students pursuant to
State regulations. The maximum number of students is determined by the square footage of

Architectural Design
The building height for the proposed development is 60 feet-9 inches. The multi-story building
is designed in a Modern architectural style that incorporates the brick from the adjacent
church with varied building materials including metals and smooth stucco. The structure will
feature metallic accents and pop-outs on the front façade to provide additional aesthetic
value and character to the proposed development.

Parking/Circulation
Parking for the proposed development will all be located on site. The development requires
163 parking spaces. The applicant proposes 119 parking spaces. Table 2 below provides a
detailed breakdown of the required parking and the number provided.

  Table 2. Parking Calculations

  Residential Visitor Parking  22 spaces  12 spaces

*Four (4) of the 69 residential spaces will be provided in tandem configuration.
**The church will meet the required parking through shared parking of 6 spaces with the pre-school.

Vehicular access to the site will be from an alley on the south side of the property into one of
three driveways. The east driveway will be 20 feet wide and provide access to the first floor
and basement level. These levels will contain 76 residential and visitor parking spaces,
including four (4) residential parking spaces in tandem configuration. The four tandem spaces
will be allotted to four (4) of the six 2-bedroom units.

Residential parking will be located primarily on the basement level with elevator access to
the first floor lobby. The pre-school and church parking will be located on the 2nd floor parking
level. The residential parking will be separated from both the required pre-school and church
parking on-site.

The center driveway will be 20 feet wide and provide access to the second floor parking area.
This level will contain 31 parking spaces: 20 church spaces including four (4) in tandem
configuration, six (6) spaces will be shared by pre-school and church and five (5) spaces will
be provided for residential visitor parking. All non-residential parking will be made available
from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Access to all after hour non-residential parking will be controlled via the
security desk in the apartment lobby.

The west driveway will be 20 feet wide and provide access to the pre-school playground
which will also be used to provide six (6) church parking spaces in tandem configuration.

The existing church located to the east of the proposed development was constructed with
38 parking spaces. The applicant is proposing to maintain 38 parking spaces for the church.
Twenty (20) parking spaces will be provided for exclusive use by the Church with 10 of these
parking spaces in tandem configuration. The Church will also enter into a covenant with the
pre-school to allow the use of 18 parking spaces to be used on Sunday when the pre-school
is closed. Six (6) of the 18 parking spaces will be in tandem configuration and located on the
pre-school playground. The church will provide valet service during church services with the
pick-up and drop-off along 85th Street.

All pedestrian access to the site will be from 85th Street via one of three walkways that
provide access to the northern, eastern, and southern entrances. Pedestrian entrances to
the preschool will be from a primary entrance off 85th Street and secondary entrance on the
western end of the building that can be accessed from 85th Street.

Vehicular pick-up and drop-off for students will be from one of two areas. The primary pick-
up and drop-off location will be from 85th Street and the secondary location will be on the
playground area. Students will be dropped off between the hours of 6:00 a.m. and 8:00 a.m.
and picked up until 6:00 p.m. Currently, all pick-up and drop-off takes place on 85th Street.
The playground area will be used for pick-up/drop-off during the hours of 6:00 a.m. to 8:00
a.m. in the mornings and 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. in the evenings Monday-Friday.

Security
The applicant is proposing to provide a security guard 24/7 onsite as well as approximately
107 interior and exterior security cameras that will be monitored in real-time throughout the
development.

Landscaping
The proposed site will consist of drought tolerant landscaping and irrigation. Landscaping
will be provided within planters along 85th Street, in the rear and side yards, and in planter
boxes on the second floor. A landscape area will also be provided on the third floor terrace.
The front planters along 85th Street will consist of a variety of plants and trees including
Marina Strawberry trees, Forest Pansy Redbuds, Fortnight Lilies, Foxtail Agave, Dwarf
Bottlefish, and Dwarf Yeddo Hawthorns. The second floor planter areas will consist of a
mixture of Spider Plant groundcovers and Variegated Flax Lilies. The third floor terrace area
will be landscaped with Wilson Fruitless Olive Trees, Iceberg Roses and will also provide
bench seating.

REQUEST
The applicant, Frank Martini, requests A Special Use Permit to allow an approximately 192
square-foot poolside bar selling 1) Beer and Wine, and 2) Distilled Spirits for on-site
consumption within an existing 80-room motel.

BACKGROUND
The Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), Chapter 12, Articles 7.1 and 25, requires approval of
a Special Use Permit (SUP) to allow the sale of alcoholic beverages for on-site consumption.

The applicant requests approval of a Special Use Permit to allow the sale of beer, wine, and
distilled spirits (State of California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Liquor
License Type 47 (On-sale General Eating Place)) for on-site consumption for a 192 square-
foot bar located within a covered breezeway on the 1st floor of an 80-room motel on a 72,758
square-foot C-2A (Airport Commercial) zoned property.

According to City records, the subject motel was constructed as a 130-unit apartment in 1958.
The swimming pool was constructed on the site in 1959. The use was subsequently
converted to a motel (Tradewinds Motel) in 1960. In 1992 the motel changed its name to the
Los Angeles Adventurer Motel and currently operates under that name. The motel also
contains a 1,825 square-foot restaurant (American Bar and Grill) and is located on the
northeast corner of the building fronting Century Boulevard. The existing restaurant has
been in existence since 1986. The existing restaurant currently has an ABC Type 47 license
for on-sale of beer, wine and distilled spirits.

On August 4, 2004, the Planning Commission approved Special Use Permit 970 (SP-970)
for the conversion of a gift shop into a 125 square-foot poolside bar with on-site sales of beer,
wine, and distilled spirits at the subject site. However, the SUP expired August 24, 2005,
since the covenant and resolution for SP-970 were never recorded. As a result, the applicant
is now returning to the Planning Commission for a similar request.

DISCUSSION
The proposed 192 square-foot bar is currently constructed but is not operating and is located
adjacent to the outdoor pool within a covered breezeway in the central courtyard of the motel.
The existing motel contains 80 rooms spread across two 2-story buildings. The building with
street frontage along Century Boulevard also contains the reception lobby, motel
administrative offices, and a car rental office. At-grade parking is spread throughout the front,
center, and rear of the property.

In addition to the 192 square-foot bar proposed for use, there is a smaller open bar with
counter, also located within the covered breezeway adjacent to the swimming pool. Per ABC
records the smaller bar served alcoholic beverages without City or ABC approval and
discontinued use in 2002. The applicant is planning to demolish the smaller bar.

The hours of operation for the proposed poolside bar are Monday through Sunday, 11:00
a.m. to 11:00 p.m. The bar will be staffed by two full-time bartenders that will work during the
proposed bar hours of operation. The bar area is equipped for a maximum of 40 persons.

The subject site has 77 parking spaces. As the proposed bar is an amenity designed to serve
motel guests, no additional parking spaces are required. Therefore, IMC parking

via Century Boulevard or two driveways along Freeman Avenue. There are no changes
proposed to the existing access. No change to the existing level of service is anticipated.

maintained.

noise, patron behavior, loitering, littering and related activities at all times. Conditions

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, October 7, 2020 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting was called
to order at 7:05 p.m., to allow the listening and watching audience
an opportunity to dial in.

to allow a five-story, 65-unit senior housing mixed–use
development on an approximately 26,250 square-foot C-2 (General
Commercial) zoned property at 3320 West 85th Street.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any

the floor for the planning commissioner’s questions via-phone-line
to the applicant.

Mr. Michael Zenon, representing Faith Lutheran, came forward and
spoke to the Planning Commission regarding his project on 85th
Street.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant a question;
 Are there any particular steps being taken to mitigate the noise
  of the children from the seniors that will be living within the
  same vicinity as the school area.
   Mr. Zenon stated that the steps have been taken to make sure
  the residential sound barrier will be in place to curtail the
  sounds of the children to not disturb the seniors who will be
  living separated from the children in the facility.

 Guest visitor parking for the seniors, what is the reason for
  the reduction of the parking spaces?
   Mr. McCrumby stated the parking provided is comparable to
  that provided in other senior developments in Inglewood.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant –
 Date of completion of this project’s construction?
   Mr. Zenon stated a total of 18 to 24 months after construction
  starts/breaks ground.

to speak for or against this project.
